# Shuyuan Shen

<p class="hero-role">Assistant Professor of Political Science and International Relations at Loyola Marymount University</p>

<p class="hero-lede">I study how media, propaganda, and political communication shape public opinion and state behavior, with a regional focus on China and a methodological focus on computational and experimental research.</p>

::: {.band-label}
## Research agenda
:::

::: {.band-copy}
My research bridges comparative politics and international relations to explain how information travels through authoritarian political systems—and what happens when domestic communication becomes global politics.
:::
:::

::: {.research-pillars}
::: {.pillar}
<span class="pillar-number">01</span>
<h3>Political communication</h3>
Propaganda, censorship, persuasion, and the political consequences of how governments communicate.
:::

::: {.pillar}
<span class="pillar-number">02</span>
<h3>Chinese politics</h3>
Domestic governance and China’s global political and economic engagement.
:::

::: {.pillar}
<span class="pillar-number">03</span>
<h3>Computational social science</h3>
Text-as-data, causal inference, meta-analysis, and survey and field experiments.
:::
:::
